newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO STOCKS END UP, WAIVER ON U.S. LONG BOND.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO STOCKS END UP, WAIVER ON U.S. LONG BOND.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended a four-day run of declines on Wednesday by finishing slightly up after a rough ride on the back of a fluctuating U.S. long bond, dealers and analysts said.
"The market is volatile in line with Wall Street, despite mild retail sales and producer prices data," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
"Fears of U.S. inflation persist and the market will be cautious until the (August 19) Fed meeting," he added.
The leading IPC share index was up 13.75 points, or 0.28 percent, at 5,016.63.

The IPC had reached as high as 5,087.31 points in early trade then dipped to a low of 4,969.11 points on profit-taking triggered by a slide on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones ended down 32.52 points at 7,928.32.

U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds, meanwhile, trimmed an early rise of 40/32 to 17/32 and a yield of 6.63 percent in late dealing. Dealers said volume of 100.1 million .TV.MX shares traded was slower than many recent sessions.
"We moved on thin volume, the market is cautious and waiting for more keynote U.S. data," a floor trader said, referring to retail price data due early on Thursday.
Dealers said falling long bond yields outweighed the effect on financial stocks of Tuesday night's increase in domestic Cetes rates.

"Cetes rate hikes are expected to be temporary," a desk trader said. Mexico's two biggest financial groups, Bancomer and Banamex-Accival, both ended up. Bancomer gained 54 centavos to 5.60 pesos, while Banamex-Accival rose 1.15 pesos to 23.90 pesos.
Cement company Cemex gained 40 centavos to 41.70 pesos as investors counted the lower cost of paying its dollar debt after the fall in long bond yields, traders said.
Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) weighed heaviest on the market, dealers said, falling five centavos to 20.20 pesos at brisk trade.
Telmex ADRs, meanwhile, shed 5/16 to end at 51-11/16.

Holding company Synkro headed the percentage gainers list .PG.MX, up nine centavos to 25. Analysts noted holders of Synkro commercial paper will be able to exchange it for stock in the company on August 21.
On the broad market, gains outnumbered declines 50 to 45, out of a total of 119 stocks that changed hands.
